name: Honeycrisp Heirloom Apple
flavorProfile: Ultra-crisp cellular snap, honeyed sweetness balanced with brisk malic tang.
culinaryUses: Raw shaved salad with pecorino and walnuts
Cider reduction glazes
Cast-iron rustic apple galettes
nutritionHighlights: High dietary soluble fiber (pectin), rich in quercetin and Vitamin C.
storageTip: Store unwashed in the crisper drawer with low humidity; stays crisp for up to 6 weeks.

name: Golden Chanterelle
flavorProfile: Apricot-like perfume, delicate velvety flesh with earthy white pepper finish.
culinaryUses: Dry sauté in brown cultured butter
Wild mushroom risotto with thyme
Folded into farm-egg French omelets
nutritionHighlights: Packed with natural Vitamin D, copper, niacin, and immune-supporting beta-glucans.
storageTip: Never wash until cooking; keep loosely wrapped in unbleached brown paper bag in the fridge.

name: Brandywine Heirloom Tomato
flavorProfile: Deeply complex heirloom sweetness with full-bodied umami acidity and tender rosy flesh.
culinaryUses: Thick slices with Maldon flake salt and olive oil
Open-face sourdough panzanella
Fresh gazpacho soup
nutritionHighlights: Abundant lycopene antioxidants, potassium, and vitamins A and K.
storageTip: Never refrigerate! Keep stem-down at room temperature out of direct sunlight.

name: Bright Lights Rainbow Chard
flavorProfile: Mild beet-like minerality in leaves with crunchy, succulent multicolored stems.
culinaryUses: Stems pickled with coriander seeds
Leaves wilted with garlic chips and golden raisins
Rustic grain frittatas
nutritionHighlights: Extremely dense in Vitamin K, lutein, magnesium, and dietary iron.
storageTip: Wrap stems in a damp paper towel and enclose in reusable silicone pouch.

name: Artisan Raw Goat Chèvre
flavorProfile: Bright citrus tang, creamy lactic acidity, delicate floral notes from mountain forage.
culinaryUses: Crumble over roasted warm beets
Spread on sourdough with wildflower honey
Stuffed into squash blossoms
nutritionHighlights: Easier to digest A2 milk proteins, bioavailable calcium, and probiotic live cultures.
storageTip: Store tightly wrapped in cheese parchment paper in the warmest section of your refrigerator.

name: Coastal Meyer Lemon
flavorProfile: Cross between true lemon and mandarin orange; aromatic edible floral zest, low bitter pith.
culinaryUses: Whole lemon quick preserves with sea salt
Meyer lemon curd tartlets
Roasted whole atop chicken and fingerling potatoes
nutritionHighlights: Exceptional Vitamin C concentration, bioflavonoids, and limonene citrus oils.
storageTip: Keeps at room temperature for 1 week; refrigerate in a perforated bag for up to a month.

name: Delicata Winter Squash
flavorProfile: Sweet brown-sugar and hazelnut custard texture with an edible, paper-thin striped skin.
culinaryUses: Roasted rings with maple and smoked paprika
Stuffed with wild rice, cranberries, and pecans
Puréed into silky autumn soup
nutritionHighlights: High in beta-carotene, Vitamin A, dietary potassium, and natural carbohydrates.
storageTip: Keep in a cool dry pantry at 50–55°F; avoids decay for up to 3 months.

name: Heritage Purple Passion Asparagus
flavorProfile: Sweeter and milder than green asparagus with nutty berry notes due to high anthocyanin pigments.
culinaryUses: Raw ribbon shaved into salads
Flash-grilled on high heat for 2 minutes
Steamed briefly and tossed with brown butter lemon
nutritionHighlights: High anthocyanins (potent flavonoids), folate, glutathione, and dietary fiber.
storageTip: Trim ends and stand upright in a glass of 1 inch cold water in the refrigerator door.

name: Wild Foraged Ramps (Wild Leeks)
flavorProfile: Pungent, sweet marriage of pungent garlic clove and spring sweet scallion.
culinaryUses: Ramp compound butter for sourdough and steaks
Fermented whole-ramp kimchi
Charred over open coals with romesco
nutritionHighlights: Choline, sulfurous allicin compounds, and Vitamin A.
storageTip: Gently clean dirt, wrap roots in damp cloth, use within 4–5 days or preserve into butter/pesto.

name: Black Mission Figs
flavorProfile: Jammy port-wine sweetness, velvety purple skin, delicate crunchy edible seeds.
culinaryUses: Paired with blue cheese and aged prosciutto
Simmered into balsamic rosemary jam
Caramelized under the broiler with labneh
nutritionHighlights: High in calcium, copper, magnesium, and dietary polyphenols.
storageTip: Extremely perishable; arrange in a single layer on a plate in refrigerator and consume within 3 days.

name: Highland Pea & Radish Microgreens
flavorProfile: Sweet snap-pea crunch or spicy radish pepper burst in miniature botanical shoots.
culinaryUses: Garnish for chilled soups and carpaccios
Piled into artisanal sourdough toasts
Blended into raw green goddess dressings
nutritionHighlights: Up to 40x higher nutrient density than mature leaves, rich in sulforaphane and Vitamin E.
storageTip: Keep roots intact in clamshell container; do not wash until moments before plating.

name: Slow-Aged Fermented Black Garlic
flavorProfile: Balsamic, tamarind, sweet licorice, soft spreadable date-like cloves with zero acrid bite.
culinaryUses: Mashed into aioli for roasted root vegetables
Black garlic vinaigrette for bitter chicory salads
Rubbed under skin of roast poultry
nutritionHighlights: Double the S-allyl-cysteine antioxidants of raw garlic, with gentle GI tolerance.
storageTip: Keep in airtight glass jar in a cool, dark cabinet; stable for over 12 months.
